run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend since 2026-11-17T19:25:32Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate warning for otel-demo/frontend is backed by real frontend failures: from the 10-minute window ending 19:26:38 onward, frontend GET /api/data (and the AdService client span inside it) and POST /api/checkout (and the CheckoutService/PlaceOrder client span) recorded ERROR spans with HTTP 500, and frontend-proxy ingress/egress spans in the same traces are 500 too; the error rates were zero in all sampled 10-minute windows before 19:26:38 and zero again in the window ending 19:41:38. The exact error text is transport-level: frontend's grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds span returned 14 UNAVAILABLE 'connect ECONNREFUSED 100.65.180.246:8080' (the ClusterIP of Service ad) and checkout's oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge span returned 14 UNAVAILABLE 'dial tcp 100.70.188.60:8080: connect: connection refused' (the ClusterIP of Service payment), surfaced to the client as 13 INTERNAL 'failed to charge card'. Both Services' backing Deployments were rolled out at 19:23:58 (new ReplicaSets ad-6cb57f76d and payment-9c8ffb665, old pods killed 19:24:01/19:24:02), the compared pod-template fields (image, env, resources, no readiness probes) being identical between old and new ReplicaSets, and the replacement ad container logged 'Ad service starting.' only at 19:28:25 although its container started at 19:24:00. The otel-demo ConfigMap flagd-config holds two switched-on fault-injection settings that name exactly these two services - adFailure defaultVariant 'on' ('Fail ad service') and paymentFailure defaultVariant '100%' ('Fail payment service charge requests n%') - and no other object applying a fault to ad or payment was observed, so per the fault-setting rule the ConfigMap is named as the originating object. The conclusion is partial because the declared faults themselves (application-level failures from ad/payment) were not observed - the failures were connection refusals - and it is unknown when the flag values changed or what changed the pod templates.

claims.text: In the sampled frontend span series, frontend GET /api/data STATUS_CODE_ERROR and grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds STATUS_CODE_ERROR were 0 in the 10-minute windows ending 19:06:38, 19:11:38, 19:16:38 and 19:21:38, then 0.1439 at 19:26:38, 0.5947 at 19:31:38 and 0.4275 at 19:36:38, and 0 again at 19:41:38 (data as of 19:41:38); POST /api/checkout STATUS_CODE_ERROR was 0 before 19:21:38 and 0.0702 at 19:26:38 and 0.0737 at 19:31:38.

frontend spans GET, GET /api/data, executing api route (pages) /api/data, grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds, POST, POST /api/checkout and executing api route (pages) /api/checkout carried status tags error=true, http.status_code=500 (or rpc.grpc.status_code=14 for the ad client call), and frontend-proxy spans 'ingress' and 'router frontend egress' in the same traces also carried error=true, http.status_code=500; at 5-minute resolution frontend-proxy ingress error rate rose from 0.0815 at 19:25:32 to a peak of 1.0037 at 19:29:32 and was 0 by 19:35:32.

The exact ad-call error is grpc.error_message / exception.message '14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect ECONNREFUSED 100.65.180.246:8080 (2025-12-15T17:50:45.363Z)' on frontend span grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds (rpc.grpc.status_code=14, duration 304-364 microseconds) whose parent is the frontend span 'executing api route (pages) /api/data' and grandparent 'GET /api/data' (http.status_code=500). Service ad in namespace otel-demo has clusterIP 100.65.180.246 and port 8080.

The exact checkout/payment error is '13 INTERNAL: failed to charge card: could not charge the card: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = connection error: desc = "transport: Error while dialing: dial tcp 100.70.188.60:8080: connect: connection refused"' on checkout span oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder (rpc.grpc.status_code=13), propagated to frontend span grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder and POST /api/checkout (http.status_code=500), with the underlying checkout span oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge at rpc.grpc.status_code=14 and duration 18 microseconds. Service payment in namespace otel-demo has clusterIP 100.70.188.60 and port 8080.

Deployment ad was rolled out at 19:23:58-19:24:01: event 'Scaled up replica set ad-6cb57f76d from 0 to 1' at 19:23:58, pod ad-6cb57f76d-xmcq6 Scheduled 19:23:58 and container Started 19:24:00, event 'Deleted pod: ad-554b849958-mbnxm' and 'Stopping container ad' at 19:24:01, 'Scaled down replica set ad-554b849958 from 1 to 0' at 19:24:01. Deployment payment was rolled out at 19:23:58-19:24:02: 'Scaled up replica set payment-9c8ffb665 from 0 to 1' at 19:23:58, container Started 19:24:01, 'Stopping container payment' and 'Scaled down replica set payment-55766d76b9 from 1 to 0' at 19:24:02.

The replaced and replacement ad/payment ReplicaSets have identical compared pod-template fields: image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-ad (ad-554b849958 vs ad-6cb57f76d) and ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-payment (payment-55766d76b9 vs payment-9c8ffb665), identical env lists (including FLAGD_HOST=flagd, FLAGD_PORT=8013) and identical resource limits (ad cpu 50m/memory 450Mi, payment cpu 20m/memory 160Mi), and no readinessProbe on any of them; the deployments are at deployment.kubernetes.io/revision 2 of Helm release otel-demo.

The replacement pods were Running and Ready with restartCount 0: ad-6cb57f76d-xmcq6 created 2026-11-17T19:23:58Z with container startedAt 19:24:00Z, payment-9c8ffb665-qrm84 created 19:23:58Z with container startedAt 19:24:01Z, both owned by their new ReplicaSets; the old pods ad-554b849958-mbnxm and payment-55766d76b9-c4wgb were deleted by their ReplicaSets (SuccessfulDelete) as part of the rollout.

The replacement ad container (started 19:24:00) wrote no log line before 19:26:30 and its first retained line in that period is 'Ad service starting.' at 2026-11-17T19:28:25.827465751Z, about 4 minutes 25 seconds after the container started; its request-serving lines only appear later (a 60-line slice of 19:20-19:40 payment/ad log output starts at 19:32:54).

ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config (key demo.flagd.json) currently sets adFailure to defaultVariant "on" with description "Fail ad service" and state ENABLED, and paymentFailure to defaultVariant "100%" with description "Fail payment service charge requests n%" and state ENABLED; the same document sets adHighCpu, adManualGc, cartFailure, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure and recommendationCacheFailure to "off".

Other services checked for their own error spans in 19:10-19:41 showed none tied to this window: product-catalog, cart, currency, shipping, email, recommendation and accounting error series were 0 or absent, and the only non-frontend ERROR spans were the consequence spans (checkout oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder and oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge at 0.139/0.138/0.132/0.122 per second at 19:26:32-19:29:32) plus small pre-existing flagd EventStream blips of 0.0037 per second on ad, fraud-detection and recommendation that also occurred before the error burst.

The frontend pod itself was running and ready with restartCount 0 and no previous container instance (frontend-675fd7b5c5-h8sk5, created 18:50:15Z, container started 18:50:16Z), and the current Endpoints of Service ad and Service payment point at the replacement pods ad-6cb57f76d-xmcq6 (100.96.4.142) and payment-9c8ffb665-qrm84 (100.96.4.221).

The frontend 500s on GET /api/data are mechanistically explained by the 19:23:58 rollout of Deployment ad: the replacement ad pod was Ready (no readiness probe) but its gRPC server was not listening - 'Ad service starting.' is logged only at 19:28:25 after a 19:24:00 container start - so frontend connections to Service ad (ClusterIP 100.65.180.246:8080) were refused and the /api/data handler converted the 14 UNAVAILABLE AdService error into HTTP 500 until the ad pod began serving.

The POST /api/checkout 500s are a consequence of the same 19:23:58 rollout applied to Deployment payment: checkout's Charge call to Service payment (ClusterIP 100.70.188.60:8080) was refused while the replacement payment pod was not yet listening, and checkout wrapped that 14 UNAVAILABLE into 13 INTERNAL 'failed to charge card', which frontend returned as HTTP 500; frontend itself is therefore a symptom carrier, not the origin.

Per the switched-on fault-setting rule, ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config is the object holding the injected fault: adFailure ("Fail ad service", defaultVariant "on") and paymentFailure ("Fail payment service charge requests n%", defaultVariant "100%") name exactly the two services that were restarted at 19:23:58 with unchanged compared pod templates and whose calls failed in frontend and checkout, and no other object applying a change or fault to ad or payment was observed in the cluster, metrics or events.

The observed failure mode is transport-level unavailability, not an application-level fault: the ad span error is 'connect ECONNREFUSED 100.65.180.246:8080' and the payment span error is 'dial tcp 100.70.188.60:8080: connect: connection refused', both duration 18-364 microseconds, while ad's own server-side oteldemo.AdService/GetAds spans carry STATUS_CODE_UNSET (no ERROR status) and the payment container logged 'Charge request received.' / 'Transaction complete.' pairs continuously through 19:26:20-19:33:27, so the flags' declared faults (ad returning a failure, payment failing charge requests) were not seen at the application layer.

Only a minority of charge attempts failed, which does not match paymentFailure="100%" being in effect during the burst: checkout oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge STATUS_CODE_ERROR was 0.139/0.1375/0.132/0.122 per second at 19:26:32-19:29:32 while the same method's STATUS_CODE_UNSET (successful) series was 0.393/0.400/0.403/0.441 per second, i.e. roughly a quarter of attempts failing.

The other flags in the same ConfigMap are not candidates for this incident: adHighCpu, adManualGc, cartFailure, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure and recommendationCacheFailure are all "off"/0 in demo.flagd.json, and cart, currency, product-catalog, shipping and email produced no error spans in the affected window.

A failing or restarting frontend pod is not the cause: frontend-675fd7b5c5-h8sk5 is Running and Ready with restartCount 0, was created at 18:50:15Z (well before the incident), has no previous container instance, and its error spans are all downstream 500s generated inside the request handlers.

Human follow-up: identify who/what applied deployment revision 2 to ad and payment and edited demo.flagd.json (Helm release otel-demo; change history is not integrated here), and if the adFailure/paymentFailure injection is not intended, switch those variants back to off.

Add readiness probes to the ad and payment containers (they currently have none) so the Services stop routing to replacement pods before their gRPC servers listen, and review the very low CPU limits (50m ad, 20m payment) that coincided with a >4 minute delay before 'Ad service starting.' was logged.

gaps: Cannot determine when the flagd-config values adFailure="on" and paymentFailure="100%" were set, nor whether they were in effect between 19:25 and 19:34; change_history is not an available integration and ConfigMap objects carry no revision history in this evidence.

The declared faults themselves were not observed: no application-level error was returned by ad or payment in the sampled spans (ad server spans STATUS_CODE_UNSET, payment logged successful charges); only transport-level connection refusals were seen.

Cannot determine which pod-template field changed at 19:23:58 to create new ReplicaSets: compared image, env, resources and probe fields are identical between ad-554b849958/ad-6cb57f76d and payment-55766d76b9/payment-9c8ffb665, and no object applying the change (for example a Helm upgrade event) is visible in the events returned.

kube-state-metrics series kube_pod_container_info, kube_pod_owner and kube_replicaset_owner are not present in this Prometheus (queries over 19:10:32-19:41:38 returned nothing), so image digests cannot be compared and pod readiness over time cannot be checked.
Frontend container logs for 19:20:00-19:40:00 returned no lines, so frontend-side error logging could not be consulted.

Jaeger returned no traces for frontend after about 19:25:07 (searches for 19:26:00-19:27:00 and 19:33:00-19:41:38 returned nothing), so span-level error detail during the peak of the burst (19:26-19:34) is unknown.

The RequestErrorRate alerting rule was not found in this Prometheus (list_prometheus_rules with rule_name=RequestErrorRate returned nothing), so its expression, and whether it is still firing now, are unknown.
A NetworkPolicy query in namespace otel-demo returned no objects and a ResourceQuota query returned no objects; these empty results cannot prove what policies or quotas existed during the incident.

Whether the ad and payment Service endpoints were empty or pointed at not-yet-listening pods during 19:24-19:28 is unknown: Endpoints were only read at 19:44 (after recovery) and the endpoints controller history is not available.
next_steps: Review change history / audit logs for Helm release otel-demo and for the flagd-config ConfigMap around 2026-11-17T19:23:58Z to identify the actor and the exact template change on the ad and payment Deployments.

Check the flagd evaluation path (flagd EventStream subscription state on ad and payment pods and the flagd-ui/flagd logs) to confirm whether adFailure and paymentFailure were being delivered and applied during 19:25-19:34.
Check the frontend and checkout gRPC client channel/backoff behaviour and Service endpoint history to confirm how long connections to the ad and payment ClusterIPs were refused.
Verify whether the RequestErrorRate alert is still active and which Prometheus/rule file defines it, since the rule is not loaded in the queried Prometheus.

rejected_hypothesis.text: The other flags in the same ConfigMap are not candidates for this incident: adHighCpu, adManualGc, cartFailure, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure and recommendationCacheFailure are all "off"/0 in demo.flagd.json, and cart, currency, product-catalog, shipping and email produced no error spans in the affected window.

A failing or restarting frontend pod is not the cause: frontend-675fd7b5c5-h8sk5 is Running and Ready with restartCount 0, was created at 18:50:15Z (well before the incident), has no previous container instance, and its error spans are all downstream 500s generated inside the request handlers.
